events.title: Republicans advancing Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act
events.summary: Republicans are advancing the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote and to vote. Only five states—Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Vermont, and Washington—have "enhanced" driver's licenses meeting the requirement; in all other states, voters would need either a passport or a birth certificate. Approximately half of Americans lack a passport, others lack birth certificates, and the names of married women who took their husband's last name and transgender Americans would not match their birth certificates. The Brennan Center for Justice found that if the measure passes, approximately 21 million Americans could lose their votes. The bill also calls for state officials to purge voter rolls.

events.title: ICE Mass Arrests Reveal 40% Had No Criminal Record

EPA received one anonymous comment expressing health and safety concerns; the Agency responded that it continually evaluates pesticides under FIFRA and the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to ensure they do not pose unreasonable risk when applied as instructed. The cancellations are effective February 10, 2026, with existing stock provisions allowing continued sale and distribution for periods ranging from one to eighteen months depending on the product.

events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency finalized approval of a no-migration variance (NMV) permitting Clean Harbors' Lone Mountain commercial hazardous waste facility in Waynoka, Oklahoma to temporarily store up to 100 treated hazardous waste "put piles" awaiting Land Disposal Restrictions (LDR) compliance verification within its Subtitle C landfill. events.title: ICE arrests through local jail cooperation reached 48 percent
events.summary: Analysis of newly released federal data by the Prison Policy Initiative shows that nearly half of all ICE arrests in the United States now occur through local jail cooperation rather than federal enforcement actions. Individuals arrested for minor offenses are automatically reported to ICE, which places detainers to hold them past their release date, funneling them into the deportation system before conviction or judicial review. States with sanctuary policies show lower rates; states with 287(g) agreements show higher rates.
events.why_relevant: The expansion of local jail cooperation with ICE creates a deportation pipeline that bypasses due process and federal oversight, concentrating enforcement power in county and municipal hands.
events.federal_nexus: ICE operates under federal immigration authority; local jails are state and county entities cooperating with federal enforcement.
events.basis: Nearly half of all ICE arrests in the United States now happen through local jail cooperation. Someone arrested for a broken taillight in Ohio or shoplifting in North Carolina or unpaid traffic tickets in Arizona goes to the local jail, where their information is automatically shared with ICE. Before they're convicted of anything and before they see a judge, ICE places a detainer asking the jail to hold them past their release date.
